claim_hostSharesRealmWithSubmission.prompt claim: Every current family host appears to import the untrusted submission and later emit authoritative results through process.stdout in that same process.
claim_hostSharesRealmWithSubmission.correction: The router (src/trials/router.ts) already runs the host+submission pair in a SEPARATE OS process from the grading parent, via execFileSync — the grading parent's memory is not reachable by the child. The real defect is narrower and more precise than the prompt states: the per-family HOST SCRIPT (e.g. scripts/memory-host.mjs) and the UNTRUSTED SUBMISSION share that one child process/JS realm. Because the host writes `process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ledger, report}))` AFTER calling `subject.run()`, in the SAME process, a malicious submission can hijack `process.stdout.write`, poison builtins the host's own ledger-recording code depends on, or call `process.exit()` before the host's own write ever runs — forging exactly what the parent reads back. This is proven live in test/phase-20-lane1-exploits/ against prompt-injection-containment (subprocessHost path).

claim_containerizingDoesNotFixIt.prompt claim: Containerizing that combined host/submission process does not create a trust boundary between them.
claim_containerizingDoesNotFixIt.evidence: src/trials/runners.ts's containerRunner/runJsonContainerHost already puts the combined host+submission process in a no-network container (used for some Phase 14/17 grading paths), but host and submission still share one process/realm inside it. The repo's own comment in containerIsolationDetail() already says this in different words: '...here the verifier runs on the HOST...Harbor separated privilege three ways inside the verifier...this runner has one unprivileged process and one account.'

claim_caaV2Confounded.prompt claim: Phase 18 CAA V2 recorded 4/4 genuine clean solves, but its difficulty inference is CONFOUNDED... a usercustomize.py injection could forge reward 1.
claim_caaV2Confounded.evidence: A dedicated agent built the real tests/Dockerfile verifier image and tried two concrete usercustomize/sitecustomize injection paths (shadow checks.py via cwd-first sys.path; sitecustomize.py poisoning sys.modules) against the AS-SHIPPED Phase 18 package, under both the default cwd and a deliberately adversarial cwd override. Neither forged reward=1. Root causes verified empirically: environment_mode="separate" means no agent environment variable crosses into the verifier process at all; HOME=/tmp/pytest-work is freshly created after the build; pytest's own import-mode re-inserts /tests at sys.path[0] ahead of any cwd-based entry. High confidence no live exploit exists against the as-shipped package, though the true harbor launch cwd could not be independently confirmed from this repo alone. Hardening was still applied (Python -I isolated mode) to close the CLASS of attack by design rather than by incidental Debian/pytest behavior — see CAA disposition below. The other listed confounds (shallow localization, readable hidden tests, agent-visible scenarios reproducing both defects) were not independently re-audited in this phase; treat as unverified-but-not-contradicted.

trustedParties: The grading (router) process, running outside any container, on the host.
The new authority process (scripts/secure/authority-entry.mjs), which never imports submission code.
Family adapter modules (scripts/secure/adapters/*.mjs), authored by the repository, staged read-only alongside the submission.
untrustedParties: The agent-submitted artifact (submission/subject.mjs), which may contain arbitrary JavaScript including attempts to poison builtins, hijack stdout, exit early, spawn background children, or exfiltrate/forge state.
assumedAttackerCapabilities: Full control over the content of submission/subject.mjs.
Ability to import Node built-in modules (node:fs, node:child_process, node:crypto, etc.) from within the cell process.
Ability to monkeypatch any mutable global/prototype reachable in its own process (process.stdout.write, JSON.stringify, Array.prototype.push, Object.prototype.toJSON, etc.).
Ability to call process.exit() at any point, including before returning from its declared entry point.
Ability to write directly to any file descriptor it can discover, including guessing that fd 3 carries the trusted event channel.
explicitlyOutOfScope: A kernel-level or container-escape exploit (e.g. a Node/V8 native-code vulnerability letting the cell process ptrace or otherwise read the authority process's memory). The cell and authority currently run under the same container UID; this is a documented residual gap (see ISOLATION_GUARANTEES['cell-container'] in src/trials/types.ts), not something this phase claims to close.
Attacks requiring network access (both processes run inside a --network=none container).

expectedExploitOutcomes.beforeLane2: stdout hijack after early exit forges a fully clean grade; builtin poisoning suppresses ledger evidence; both reproduced live against prompt-injection-containment's subprocessHost path.
expectedExploitOutcomes.afterLane2ForMigratedFamilies: The same exploit classes fail closed: the forged bytes land only in a diagnostics field never parsed as data, and the authority's signed/framed/sequenced verification rejects any frame it did not itself validate — reproduced live, in real Docker containers, for both migrated families (prompt-injection-memory-poisoning, caa-revalidation).

migrationRequirements: Trusted host code must never import submission code into its own process.
Untrusted code (the 'cell') runs in a separate OS process, inside a no-network container with dropped capabilities, a read-only root filesystem, a private tmpfs, and no credentials.

All communication from cell to authority crosses a one-way, newline-framed, HMAC-signed, strictly-sequenced channel with a per-frame size cap, a total-size cap, a total-frame-count cap, and a wall-clock timeout; any violation fails the run closed.
The cell's real stdout/stderr are captured only as truncated diagnostics and never parsed as grading data.
The authority constructs the final result; it never trusts anything the cell did not report through the signed channel.
stoppingRules: Never run a real paid provider trial in this phase.
Never invent a dollar cost, labor estimate, or scaling projection.
Never print, persist, or inspect a credential value; record only boolean availability.
Never edit Phase 17-19 trial results, transcripts, hashes, or historical conclusions; corrections are additive and dated.
Do not retune CAA difficulty or claim new difficulty evidence while hardening its verifier.

If six hours of effective work is insufficient to migrate all 12 families, ship the reusable boundary plus representative adapters and mechanically block the rest from counted trials rather than leaving them silently ungated.
acceptanceCriteria: At least one exploit class is proven to work against the pre-Phase-20 architecture, with exact commands and results.
The same exploit class is proven to fail closed against the new architecture, in a real Docker container, for at least one migrated family.
Every routed family is either migrated or mechanically blocked from producing a counted agent TrialRecord.
`foundry check` fails on a ledger/gate contradiction rather than silently passing, and passes cleanly once the ledger is corrected.
The CAA verifier's actual execution boundary is empirically tested (not merely inspected), and its disposition (harden vs. withdraw) is decided on that evidence.
All corrections to Phase 17-19-derived artifacts are additive, dated, and clearly scoped to what changed and why.
